analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, the CLI patch, release-guide head excerpt, and CLI base context against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. The changes document explicit local rollback, quarantine of the displaced release, confirmation/noninteractive consent, lifecycle draining and forced interruption, update-lease serialization, predecessor identity checks, and refusals for cluster or unmanaged providers (docs/provider/cli-reference.md head 743–769). docs/operations/provider-release.md:1033–1044 distinguishes local restoration from release deactivation and permanent build revocation; it does not instruct operators to bypass serving authorization. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation changes.
Integration must verify the documented contracts in provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/UpdateRollback.swift and ProviderCore/Update/SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift: plan/install-generation revalidation, retained predecessor hash/signature verification, lease coverage through journaled swapping, drain/usage settlement, restart/watchdog behavior, and quarantine persistence. These relate to T-043, T-010, T-053, T-054 and privileged-helper lease teardown (T-047). Local offline installation must not be mistaken for renewed coordinator authorization. The rollback implementation and unchanged callers are not supplied here, so those controls are unverified, not observed missing controls. Existing CLI cache/media, attestation, token and lifecycle descriptions were examined as context; this patch provides no evidence of changes to encryption, cache scoping (T-041), credentials, inference data exposure or billing.
